title: the DSG Deepearth areas 6-7

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 6-7, R536: printed pp. 81-82 (pdf 82-83) - the individual area key reaches the old dead heart of Deepearth and its great chasm: Area 6 Caverns of the Ancients (the small cave series showing considerable excavation and decoration - the single 30-ft-wide, 10-ft-ceiling entry tunnel leading to the huge domed chamber nearly 1/2 mile across, its massive stone columns, and the elaborate bestial temple at the exact center; the concentric rings of two- and three-story stone buildings with their wide smooth avenues and the crude stone barracks of the cavern wall; the tall palace with its elegantly thin columns and its huge shut brass doors - the only closed doorways in the city - and the hundreds of rooms branching from the facade towering 100 feet high and 300 feet to either side; the five additional tunnels at 60-degree intervals, once the city's farmland and now uniformly dusty and empty; the duergar builders driven deeper by the water-table shift that dried their wells, leaving not a single living creature or plant; the palace honor guard of hundreds of zombies, skeletons and mummified leaders that attacks when the doors open and pursues only to the Area 6/7 tunnel juncture; the centuries-stale dry air that stops the exerting after 2d6 rounds with 1d6-round recoveries; the stripped stone furniture, the fragile crumbling wood, the fungus farms and cave-pig corrals gone to dust; and the secret palace-hall trapdoor to the smithy - the extinguished furnaces, the massive black 25,000-gp forge-of-power anvil with its +1 enchantments, and the +2/+3 weapons possible with a hammer of substance), and Area 7 Grand Canyon of Deepearth (the yawning chasm over ten miles long and fully a mile wide, its naturally arched 200-ft ceiling at the Area 6 entrance; the walls meeting in the boulder-and-rubble gorge over a mile below; the water-erosion origin and the great river that died with the duergar wells; the old, generally stable, crack-and-ledge-riddled rock with no bridges at this height; the hidden cavern series 3,000 feet down and two miles south of the upper tunnels; the limestone cave mouths as deep as 300 feet at their 500-ft intervals; the 1-to-3-ft vertical shafts to the surface city's sewers, useless to all but bats; the great bat numbers with their several hundred mobats attacking in 2d6 groups; the cave fishers, the pair of giant slugs scouring the bottom, the giant centipedes and the wall-crawling carrion crawlers; the two dozen cloakers of the highest caves, 50% drawn to mobat combats to finish the wounded; the stagnant unfed pools with their 50% disease chance; and the sparse wall-niche lichens and fungi)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~10303-10463) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 372-376 = the printed pp. 81-83 windows); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the 30-ft tunnel with its 10-ft ceiling, the half-mile dome, the 100/300-ft facade, the 60-degree intervals and five tunnels, the 2d6/1d6 air rounds, the 25,000-gp anvil with its +1 and +2/+3 bonuses, the ten-mile canyon, the 200-ft ceiling, the mile-deep gorge, the 3,000-ft and two-mile hidden caverns, the 300-ft cave mouths at 500-ft intervals, the 1-to-3-ft shafts, the 2d6 mobat groups, the 50% cloaker draw, the two dozen cloakers and the 50% pool-disease chance; the only garbles are non-load-bearing (the djvu '5096' for the 50% chance and the Capture 'ld6' for 1d6, each settled by the other read, plus the 'balancc' and 'ofpowerof' spacing noise). SEAMS: the Monster Manual denizens (the duergar, the undead host, the mobats, cave fishers, giant slugs, centipedes, carrion crawlers and cloakers), the PHB cause disease spell and the hammer of substance, the duergar forge-of-power magic, and the R503 re-grain. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533/R534/R535 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the entry-tunnel width and ceiling, the dome, facade and tunnel intervals, the air-stress dice, the anvil's weight and enchantment bonuses, the canyon's dimensions and depths, the cave-mouth sizes and intervals, the shaft diameters, the mobat dice, the cloaker odds and the pool-disease chance, with the 2d6/1d6/2d6 dice pinned as count-and-sides const pairs. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The MM/PHB/forge/R503 seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnaeEntryTunnelWidthFt
consts.comment: the single entry tunnel of the ancient city was smoothed and widened to a uniform width of 30 feet.

consts.name: dnaeEntryTunnelCeilFt
consts.comment: the entry tunnel has a uniform ceiling of 10 feet along its length.

consts.name: dnaeDomeDiaHalfMile
consts.comment: the entry corridor leads to a huge, domed chamber nearly 1/2 mile in diameter; massive stone columns support the ceiling and an elaborate temple carved with bestial shapes stands at the exact center.

consts.name: dnaePalaceFacadeHtFt
consts.comment: at the end opposite the entrance tunnel stands the tall palace; its facade towers fully 100 feet high.

consts.name: dnaePalaceFacadeSideFt
consts.comment: the palace facade stretches for 300 feet to either side of the main entrance, with hundreds of rooms branching out.

consts.name: dnaeTunnelIntervalDeg
consts.comment: at 60-degree intervals about the circular walls of the cavern, five additional tunnels branch out to smaller caverns.

consts.name: dnaeSideTunnelCount
consts.comment: five additional tunnels branch out from the circular cavern walls to the smaller side caverns - now uniformly dusty and empty, though they once served as farmland for the city's residents.

consts.name: dnaeAirStopDice
consts.comment: no fresh air has entered this region for centuries; characters exerting themselves have to stop, gasping, after 2d6 rounds (the die count).

consts.name: dnaeAirStopSides
consts.comment: exertion in the stale air forces a stop after 2d6 rounds (the die sides).

consts.name: dnaeAirRecoverDice
consts.comment: recovery from gasping in the dead air takes 1d6 rounds (the die count).

consts.name: dnaeAirRecoverSides
consts.comment: recovery from gasping in the dead air takes 1d6 rounds (the die sides).

consts.name: dnaeAnvilWeightGp
consts.comment: the massive black anvil at the center of the secret smithy weighs 25,000 gp.

consts.name: dnaeAnvilBonus
consts.comment: any weapons or armor hammered into shape upon the duergar forge-of-power anvil gain an enchantment bonus of +1; this cannot be used to improve an existing weapon.

consts.name: dnaeAnvilHammerLow
consts.comment: when the anvil is combined with the hammer of substance wielded by a dwarven or duergar smith, weapons of +2 enchantment can be created (the low bound).

consts.name: dnaeAnvilHammerHigh
consts.comment: with the hammer of substance, weapons of even +3 enchantment can be created (the high bound).

consts.name: dnaeCanyonLenMiles
consts.comment: the yawning chasm of the Grand Canyon stretches over ten miles in length.

consts.name: dnaeCanyonWidthMiles
consts.comment: the canyon is fully a mile wide.

consts.name: dnaeCanyonCeilFt
consts.comment: the naturally arching ceiling is about 200 feet high at the point where the tunnel from Area 6 enters.

consts.name: dnaeGorgeDepthMiles
consts.comment: the canyon walls gradually grow closer together as they descend, meeting in a boulder-and-rubble-filled gorge over a mile below.

consts.name: dnaeLowerCavernsDepthFt
consts.comment: about 3,000 feet below the access-tunnel level, another series of caverns enters the canyon on one side and continues out the other.

consts.name: dnaeLowerCavernsSouthMiles
consts.comment: the lower cavern series lies about two miles south of the upper-level tunnels, so characters scaling straight down the walls do not discover them.

consts.name: dnaeCaveMouthDeepFt
consts.comment: the canyon walls are pockmarked regularly with limestone caves, some of them as deep as 300 feet.

consts.name: dnaeCaveMouthIntervalFt
consts.comment: the limestone cave mouths occur at intervals of about 500 feet above, below, and to the sides of each other - sometimes closer, sometimes more widely separated.

consts.name: dnaeShaftDiaLowFt
consts.comment: at the cavern ceiling several narrow vertical shafts lead up to join a major tunnel connecting with the sewer system of the large surface city; they range from 1-3 feet in diameter (the low bound).

consts.name: dnaeShaftDiaHighFt
consts.comment: the vertical shafts range from 1-3 feet in diameter and often climb straight up, of little use to any creatures except bats (the high bound).

consts.name: dnaeMobatGroupDice
consts.comment: several hundred mobats live in the canyon and aggressively attack large warm-blooded intruders, but in groups of 2d6 at a time (the die count).

consts.name: dnaeMobatGroupSides
consts.comment: the mobats attack in groups of 2d6 at a time (the die sides).

consts.name: dnaeCloakerAttractPct
consts.comment: the cloakers of the highest side caves are 50% likely to be attracted if the mobats attack an intruder; they fly to the combat scene and wait for the bats to drive off or claim their victim.

consts.name: dnaeCloakerCount
consts.comment: the cloaker community numbers about two dozen individuals; they do not attack as a group, and the number used should be balanced with the levels of the player characters.

consts.name: dnaePoolDiseasePct
consts.comment: the stagnant canyon-bottom pools receive no fresh flowing water; characters who drink from them have a 50% chance of contracting a disease, as in the cause disease spell effect.

bools.name: dnaeExcavatedCity
bools.comment: this relatively small series of caves shows considerable evidence of excavation and decoration: the concentric rings of two- and three-story stone buildings around the bestial temple, separated by wide smooth avenues, with a ring of crude stone barracks in the cavern wall providing the only simple quarters in the ancient city.

bools.name: dnaeBrassDoors
bools.comment: the tall palace stands surrounded by elegantly thin columns, and its huge brass doors stand shut - the only closed doorways in the city.

bools.name: dnaeDuergarExodus
bools.comment: the original builders of the city were the duergar; shifts in the water table centuries ago dried up their wells and forced the race to migrate deeper underground, and now not a single creature or plant lives in the area.

bools.name: dnaeUndeadHonorGuard
bools.comment: an honor guard of undead stands at attention around the massive hall of the palace - hundreds of zombies, skeletons, and mummified leaders arrayed to lead the host to battle; if the palace doors are opened the orders to attack are given, and the undead pursue a foe only to the juncture of the Area 6 and Area 7 tunnels.

bools.name: dnaeDeadAirDry
bools.comment: the area is completely dry - not so much as a cup of water - and the stale air smells faintly of decay and is of very poor quality.

bools.name: dnaeStrippedFragile
bools.comment: virtually all items of value were stripped from the city by the duergar upon their emigration; stone furniture is common, but the few surviving wooden items are fragile and quickly crumble under pressure, and the side caverns that once raised edible fungus and corralled cave-pigs and other livestock now hold only a thick layer of dust over dry soil.

bools.name: dnaeForgeOfPower
bools.comment: a secret trapdoor in the floor of the great palace hall leads to a large smithy: great furnaces long since extinguished line the walls, and the massive black anvil at the center radiates strong magic - it is the forge of power of the duergar.

bools.name: dnaeCanyonErosionOrigin
bools.comment: the canyon was originally excavated by water erosion - a great river once cut a path through it, and the same shift in water table that dried up the duergar wells caused the river to cease flowing; it is now similar to a dead cave with few formations, kept less dusty by faint circulating breezes, and it has withstood many a tumultuous earthquake.

bools.name: dnaeStableWalls
bools.comment: the canyon walls are cracked and riddled with ledges, chimneys and other irregularities, but the rock is old and generally stable - not likely to break off when climbed; no bridges cross it at this height.

bools.name: dnaeBatSwarms
bools.comment: bats inhabit the canyon in great numbers, most of the harmless normal varieties; the several hundred mobats subsist off the former but also aggressively attack large warm-blooded intruders, though not all together.

bools.name: dnaeCanyonPredators
bools.comment: several of the small caves branching off the canyon are the lairs of cave fishers that strike any flying or climbing creatures within reach; the canyon bottom is regularly scoured by a pair of giant slugs, many smaller side caves house giant centipedes, and carrion crawlers regularly move up and down the walls.

bools.name: dnaeStagnantPools
bools.comment: the canyon has a plentiful supply of fresh air from its access tunnels, but water is confined to a number of stagnant pools among the rocks at the bottom - some very large and deep, none fed by fresh flowing water.

bools.name: dnaeCanyonFood
bools.comment: food supplies are limited to the creatures living here and a few lichens and fungi growing in narrow niches upon the canyon walls.

examples.note: the canyon's hidden depths: the 3,000-ft-down, 2-miles-south caverns, the 300-ft cave mouths at 500-ft intervals, the 1-to-3-ft sewer shafts.
